brief: Six tools that only earn their place under load

slots.eyebrow: Everything works fine on a good day
slots.headlineLine2: is not the one you tested.
slots.subline: Six tools, and the specific way each one behaves when the day goes wrong.
slots.coverNote: Every failure below happened to somebody in a normal week

slots.title: It will not warn you before it stops
slots.body: Connection limits are reached silently and then all at once. The database is fine; the pool in front of it is what fails, and it fails at exactly the moment traffic proves you were right about something.
slots.insightText: Set the pool size before you need it, not during.

slots.title: A cache that never misses is a liability
slots.body: It works until an eviction, a restart or a deploy empties it, and then every request arrives at the database at once. The cache was load-bearing and nobody wrote that down.
slots.insightText: Test with the cache empty, on purpose, before it happens.

slots.title: The fastest response is the one you never send
slots.body: Most traffic is the same handful of requests. Serving them at the edge removes the origin from the equation entirely, which is the only optimisation that gets cheaper as you grow.
slots.insightText: Cache the boring paths first. They are most of the bill.

slots.title: It runs here is not a claim about anywhere else
slots.body: The image pins the code and almost nothing else. Clock, locale, memory limit and file descriptors all come from the host, and every one of them has taken down a production service.
slots.insightText: Set the memory limit explicitly. The default is the host's.

slots.title: A green build is a claim, not a proof
slots.body: Tests run against a database nobody uses, with data nobody has, on a machine with no other traffic. Green means it did not fail in that specific fiction, which is worth something but not what people take it for.
slots.insightText: Run one check against production after every deploy.

slots.title: None of these failed on their own
slots.body: Every outage here needed two things to go wrong at once, which is why each component looked fine in isolation and why the post-mortem always finds a cause nobody could have prioritised beforehand.
slots.insightText: Practise the recovery. You cannot predict the cause.

slots.eyebrow: Pick the one you have never tested
slots.headline: Break it
slots.subline: Empty the cache, kill a container, pull a connection. On a quiet afternoon it is an experiment; at 3 a.m. it is an incident.
slots.signoff: The recovery is the only part you control
